commit_attribution: The primary human-authorized operator session performed Section-0 governance validation (branch/HEAD/origin-main/clean-tree confirmation, predecessor reconciliation cross-check across PROJECT_STATUS.md/metadata.json/latest report, genuine-Linux-host reachability confirmation via ssh hac-dell) and independent CPIPC derivation via pcae.core.phase_id (is_valid True, same_series/same_branch True, compare=less, equals=False, unique against git log --all) before task creation. Dispatched one bounded, isolated general-purpose worker with explicit no-finalization-authority constraints (no src/pcae/** edits, no commit, no push, no pcae phase complete) to perform the bulk of the adversarial Linux verification work on hac-dell: Repair A/B reconstruction, exec-inheritance/fd-isolation/path-substitution/symlink-digest tests, Finding C empirical classification, REAL/NON_REAL profile-selection and entrypoint attacks, certification_read/ceremony_entry real-store end-to-end tests, REQ-033 writer-mint search, SO_PEERCRED and transitive-import attacks, replay/framing regression, and the predecessor test-template diff adjudication. The primary operator then independently re-verified every load-bearing claim before accepting it rather than trusting the worker's report: re-derived the repair commit and its ancestry to HEAD directly via git; independently re-ran the new IV test file and the full predecessor regression suite on hac-dell in a separately-provisioned venv (not the worker's); read the full new test file and confirmed its assertions are genuinely adversarial (real subprocess as a second unprivileged uid, real socket connect attempts, real PYTHONPATH/cwd shadow modules); independently re-hashed all three contract files and confirmed byte-identity; independently re-checked REQ-033 via a corrected grep (the first grep pass over-matched prose/docstrings disclaiming the import, not actual import statements -- caught and corrected before acceptance); independently reproduced the disclosed mislabeled predecessor test's failure and root-caused it directly by reading the test source. The primary operator then performed the full governed finalization lifecycle: task activation/scope widening, two governed commits, governed fast-green attribution (three isolated-rerun classification passes to correctly resolve two order/state-dependent nodes -- a pre-push HEAD-vs-origin-main node and a known shared-audit-directory node also independently disclosed by the predecessor CPIPC phase), governed push, final post-push fast-green attribution (PASS, 0 attributable failures), and this canonical report/metadata/PROJECT_STATUS.md update, commit, push, and completion notification.
summary: Fresh, independent, genuine-Linux (hac-dell, Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 7.0.0) verification of the N16-5-F-5-TB-REAL-HELPER-BOUNDARY-REPAIR commit (43813b16). Independently reconstructed Repair A (os.set_inheritable + /proc/self/fd exec, hpac_pawa_helper_os.py::execute_verified) and Repair B (REAL/NON_REAL canonical-store profile wiring, hpac_pawa_helper_entrypoint.py) directly from current source. Adjudicated both items the predecessor CPIPC-reconciliation phase left open: Finding C (in-place same-inode content mutation) disposed as C-A -- not exploitable under governed deployment invariants, empirically confirmed via a genuine second unprivileged OS principal (uid 65534/nobody) that cannot open the verified inode for writing (EACCES) and cannot even connect to the private one-shot channel socket; only the deployment-owner uid, already the maximal trust principal this boundary's own peer authentication exists to admit, can reach the mutation. The predecessor test-file template change (in test_n16_5_f_5_tb_real_helper_store_launcher_impl.py) disposed as T-A -- legitimate fixture update, coverage relocated and, on inspection, broadened by new main()-level adversarial tests the same repair commit added. Five new fresh IV tests written (tests/test_n16_5_f_5_tb_real_helper_boundary_repair_iv.py) covering the two gaps the predecessor's 60-test suite left untested: Finding C against a genuine non-owner principal, and a transitive-import attack (hostile PYTHONPATH / cwd-shadow module) against the real end-to-end launch_and_exchange path. All subsystem verdicts (exec inheritance, fd isolation, path substitution, symlink/digest attacks, REAL profile selection, certification_read/ceremony_entry real-store wiring, blocked writes, REQ-033, SO_PEERCRED, transitive import, replay, framing) independently VERIFIED by the primary operator, not merely accepted from the delegated worker. One new, non-security finding disclosed: predecessor test test_helper_substitution_after_verification_is_rejected uses Path.write_bytes() on the verified path, which mutates the SAME inode in place rather than swapping the directory entry -- it is actually re-testing Finding C's already-disclosed gap under a directory-entry-substitution label, and fails deterministically on real Linux (independently reproduced); not fixed, out of this phase's file-touch scope, flagged for a future narrow test-repair phase. Zero production source, contract, schema, dependency, or packaging change. N-16-5 remains NOT CLOSED. Recommended next: a narrow, human-authorized helper writer-authority contract architecture/evolution phase to close the admin_mutation/certification_write/presentation_evidence_write blocker -- NOT begun.

(8) contract baselines -- `sha256sum` re-run directly by the primary operator on all three contract files, byte-identical to the worker's reported hashes; (9) fast-green attribution -- run by the primary operator directly (not delegated), three times: first pass post-first-commit found the pre-push HEAD-vs-origin-main node attributable (expected, resolved by pushing) plus the known shared-audit-directory node;
